'''GR 8''' (also known as '''UGC 8091''') is a gas-rich [[dwarf irregular galaxy]].<ref name="Tolstoy1999">{{cite book
  | author=Tolstoy, Eline
  | chapter=Detailed Star-Formation Histories of Nearby Dwarf Irregular Galaxies using HST
  | title = The stellar content of Local Group galaxies, Proceedings of the 192nd symposium of the International Astronomical Union
  | year=1999
  | volume=192
 | pages=218
  | bibcode=1999IAUS..192..218T
  | isbn = 1886733821
  | publisher = [[Astronomical Society of the Pacific]]
  |editor1= Patricia Whitelock |editor2=Russell Cannon
  }}</ref>
In 1995, Tolstoy et al. estimated its distance (with the [[Hipparcos]] correction of 1997 applied) to be approximately {{convert|7.9|e6ly}} from Earth. It is around 2.8 [[light-year|Mly]] from [[UGC 9128]].<ref name="ddo187">{{cite journal |title=Aparicio, Tikhonov, & Karachentsev, DDO 187 |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/301157/fulltext/990200.text.html#sc4 |journal=[[Astronomical Journal]] |access-date=8 August 2021 |doi=10.1086/301157|s2cid=15309075 |arxiv=astro-ph/9909493 |last1=Aparicio |first1=A. |last2=Tikhonov |first2=N. |last3=Karachentsev |first3=I. |date=1999 }}</ref> It is still an open question whether it is a member of the [[Local Group]] or possibly the [[Virgo Cluster]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GR 8 |url=http://spider.seds.org/spider/LG/gr8.html |access-date=2023-04-30 |website=spider.seds.org}}</ref>  

GR 8 was discovered at the [[Lick Observatory]] using the 20-inch [[astrograph]] in either 1946, 1947, or 1951.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Reaves |first1=G. |title=Dwarf galaxies in the Virgo cluster |journal=The Astronomical Journal |date=1956 |volume=61 |page=69 |doi=10.1086/107292 |bibcode=1956AJ.....61...69R}}</ref>
